transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I came in because flying has gotten, uh, honestly unbearable. Just the thought of getting on an airplane now scares me so bad. I know, rationally, it doesn’t make sense — I mean, I’m a physician, I know the statistics, I’ve told other people not to worry about things that are rare — but when it’s me, my body just… it tells me that plane is going to fall.

And then I start thinking about airports, boarding, all that, and it’s like my mind runs off with it. I used to watch those flight boards when I was younger, you know, all the cities listed, and think it was exciting. Now I look at a plane and I just feel like, no, absolutely not. It’s embarrassing to even say out loud.
Is this fear mainly only about flying?

Yes… mainly flying. It’s really the airplane itself, the idea of getting on it. I can tell myself all day that it doesn’t make sense, that planes are safe, but the second I picture being on one, my body just reacts like it knows the plane is going to fall.

It’s funny, I used to love airports as a kid—those big boards with all the cities, imagining where people were going—but now that same setting just points me right back to the plane. So, yeah, it’s about flying.
When you think about flying or are near a plane, do you ever suddenly get a surge of intense panic?

Yes. It’s pretty immediate, actually. Even if it’s not like I’m standing at the gate or anything—sometimes I’ll just get an email about a rural shift that would require a flight, and right away my heart starts pounding. My hands get sweaty, and I feel like I can’t breathe until I close the message.

Which is ridiculous, because it’s just an email, you know? I get a hundred emails a day, most of them are nonsense about scheduling or hospital policy changes, and normally I just skim and move on. But if it has anything to do with flying, it’s like my body reacts before I’ve even really thought it through.
Do these intense panic surges ever happen when you’re not thinking about flying or anything related to it?

Not really… I mean, the big surges seem tied to flying, or something that reminds me of it. Like even if it’s just an email about a rural shift where I’d have to fly, my heart starts pounding right away, my hands get sweaty, and I feel like I can’t breathe until I close the message.

It’s strange, because I can handle all kinds of stressful messages for work, scheduling stuff, patient issues, all of that—but if it implies getting on a plane, my body just reacts.
